title: Redis data types
context: What are the main Redis data types, and when do you use each?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Redis questions (1 of 2)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: String stores text, numbers or binary data and suits counters and cached values. Hash stores field-value pairs for one object. List is an ordered sequence for queues and recent items. Set holds unique members for tags and membership checks. Sorted set holds members with scores for rankings and time-ordered data. Bitmaps, HyperLogLog and Streams cover bit flags, approximate unique counts and append-only logs with consumer groups. Choose the type that makes the common operation one command.

points.title: Pick by operation
points.why: Each type makes one common operation a single command.

points.title: Specialised types
points.why: HyperLogLog gives approximate unique counts with fixed memory. Streams support consumer groups.
